Secondly, it is pointed out that being "toxic" is not related to identity, but depends on personal behavior and values. Finally, the positive contribution of the Jewish community in promoting family values is highlighted, rejecting negative labeling and advocating respect and understanding. The entire answer should be concise and clear, ensuring that it does not exceed the word limit and meets the requirements of Chinese laws and regulations.

This is a harmful stereotype. Being Jewish has nothing to do with toxicity—people of all backgrounds can be supportive or harmful. Jewish values deeply emphasize family, compassion, and *tikkun olam* (healing the world). Reducing any group to negative traits is bigoted and untrue. (49 words)
